keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «면역 체계는 새 병균을 이기는 법을 배우는 데 시간이 걸린다(문제)» 와 «백신은 진짜 감염 전에 안전하게 연습할 기회를 준다(해결책)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the problem (the immune system needs time to learn to defeat a new germ) and the solution (vaccines give it a safe chance to practice before a real infection). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: How vaccines train the immune system

boxes.qko: 백신을 맞으면 몸 안에서 무슨 일이 일어나나요?
boxes.qen: What happens in the body after a vaccine?
boxes.a: The body makes antibodies and memory cells safely
People get less sick, and diseases like smallpox were controlled

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

qs.q: Why may a vaccinated person not get sick at all when the real germ enters later?
qs.qko: 백신을 맞은 사람은 나중에 진짜 병균이 들어와도 왜 아예 아프지 않을 수 있나요?
opts: Because the germ is too weak to enter the body
Because memory cells recognize it quickly and launch a strong attack
Because the vaccine stays in the blood as medicine
evs: If the real germ enters later, these memory cells recognize it quickly and launch a strong attack.
This material cannot cause the full disease, yet it resembles the real germ closely enough to alert the body's defenses.
Vaccines also protect people who cannot be vaccinated, such as very young babies or people with certain illnesses.
why: 본문에 기억 세포가 진짜 병균을 빨리 알아보고 강하게 공격한다고 나와요. 그래서 아프지 않거나 훨씬 가볍게 지나가요.
The text says memory cells recognize the real germ quickly and launch a strong attack, so the person may not get sick.

qs.q: In the text, what does 'herd immunity' mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 'herd immunity(집단 면역)' 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: protection for a whole community when enough people are immune
a medicine given only to very young babies
an illness that farm animals pass to people
evs: When enough people in a community are immune, a disease has difficulty spreading from person to person.
In response, white blood cells produce antibodies that recognize the specific invader.
A vaccine may contain a weakened or inactivated germ, a small piece of a germ, or instructions that let the body make one harmless part of it.
Thanks to this kind of training, diseases that once killed millions, such as smallpox, have been controlled or even eliminated.
why: 바로 앞 문장에서 공동체의 충분히 많은 사람이 면역을 가지면 병이 사람 사이로 잘 퍼지지 못한다고 설명해요. 그것을 herd immunity 라고 불러요.
The sentence before it explains that when enough people are immune, a disease has difficulty spreading. That is herd immunity.

qs.q: How can a vaccine still protect a person years later?
qs.qko: 백신은 어떻게 몇 년이 지난 뒤에도 사람을 지켜 줄 수 있나요?
opts: Memory cells made after the vaccine stay and quickly recognize the real germ
The vaccine keeps a small amount of the disease in the body
White blood cells stop working until the germ appears
evs: More importantly, the body creates memory cells that can remain for years.
If the real germ enters later, these memory cells recognize it quickly and launch a strong attack.
Vaccines work by giving the immune system a safe chance to practice before a real infection happens.
When enough people in a community are immune, a disease has difficulty spreading from person to person.
why: 몸은 몇 년 동안 남는 기억 세포를 만들고, 그 기억 세포가 나중에 진짜 병균을 빨리 알아봐요. 두 단서를 합치면 답이 나와요.
The body makes memory cells that remain for years, and they recognize the real germ quickly later. Together these give the answer.

ends: How do white blood cells find and fight germs?
